title: Comparing: 比, 没有, 最, 这么 and 那么
explain: To say A is more than B, put 比 between them and the adjective after: 他比我高 means 'He is taller than me'. Do not add 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence.
To say how much more, put the amount after the adjective: 他比我大三岁 'He is three years older than me'; 这个比那个好一点 'This one is a bit better than that one'; 他比我高多了 'He is much taller than me'.
To say A is not as ... as B, use 没有: 我没有他高 'I am not as tall as he is'. Add 那么 to say 'so': 我没有他那么高.
最 means 'most': 我最喜欢茶 'I like tea most'. 这么 and 那么 mean 'so': 这么贵 'so expensive' (this much, about something near), 那么远 'so far' (that much, about something farther away).

examples.en: He is taller than me.
My older brother is three years older than me.
I am not as tall as he is.
I like playing soccer most.

mistakes: Do not put 很 (or 非常, 太) in a 比 sentence. Say 他比我高, not 他比我很高.

q.en: My older sister is taller than me.
q.explain: A + 比 + B + adjective.

q.en: Today is colder than yesterday.
q.explain: 比 goes between the two things you compare.

q.en: I am not as tall as him.
q.explain: 没有 says A is not as ... as B.

q.en: My younger sister is taller than me.
q.explain: Do not put 很 in a 比 sentence.

q.en: I like this watch best.
q.explain: 最 goes before the verb 喜欢.

title: Distance and direction: 离, 从…到… and 往
explain: 离 measures the distance between two places. Put it between them and finish with 远 or 近: 学校离我家很近 'The school is close to my home'. Add 很 before 近 or 远, or 不 for the negative: 不远.
从…到… means 'from … to …', for places and for times: 从我家到学校 'from my home to school'; 从八点到十点 'from eight to ten'. 从 on its own says where something starts: 我从学校回来 'I come back from school'.
往 means 'toward' and is used for directions: 往左走 'go to the left', 往前走 'go forward'.

examples.en: The school is close to my home.
The airport is far from here.
I walk from home to school.

examples.zh: 请往左走，洗手间在右边。
examples.en: Please go left; the restroom is on the right.

mistakes: Keep the pattern place + 离 + place + 很远. Do not say 学校很远我家, the way English says 'the school is far from my home'.

q.en: The shop is not far from my home.
q.explain: 离 sits between the two places, then 不远.

q.en: We walk to the right.
q.explain: 往 + direction + 走.

q.en: My home is close to school.
q.explain: 离 goes between the two places.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I work from Monday to Friday?
options: 我从星期一到星期五上班。
我离星期一到星期五上班。
q.zh: 我从星期一到星期五上班。
q.en: I work from Monday to Friday.
q.explain: 从…到… gives the start and the end.

q.en: I work from eight to five.
q.explain: 从 marks the start, 到 marks the end.

title: 到 and 在 after a verb
explain: 到 before a place means 'arrive at' or 'go to': 我们到机场了 'We have arrived at the airport'. 他每天八点到学校 'He gets to school at eight every day'.

Most verbs keep 在 + place before the verb (我在家吃饭), but a few verbs take 在 + place after them to say where the person ends up: 我住在学校旁边 'I live next to the school'; 她站在门口 'She is standing at the door'. Common ones are 住, 坐 and 站.
Compare 我在这里工作 (the working happens here) and 我住在这里 (I live here).

examples.en: We have arrived at the airport.
He gets to school at eight every day.
I live next to the school.
She is standing at the door waiting for you.

mistakes: Most verbs keep 在 + place before the verb: 我在学校学习, not 我学习在学校. Only a few verbs such as 住, 坐 and 站 take 在 + place after them.

q.en: I live next to the hospital.
q.explain: 住 + 在 + place: 在 comes right after 住.

q.en: They are sitting in the classroom.
q.explain: 坐 + 在 + place.

q.en: Mom got home at six.
q.explain: 到 + place means to arrive at.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Grandma lives at my home?
q.en: Grandma lives at my home.
q.explain: After 住 you need 在 before the place.

q.en: He has arrived at school.
q.explain: 到 already means arrive at; do not add 在.

title: 过: have done it before
explain: Put 过 after a verb to say you have done it at least once in your life: 我去过中国 'I have been to China'. This 过 is pronounced guo with a light tone, and the verb does not change.
To say you have never done it, use 没 + verb + 过: 我没吃过这个 'I have never eaten this'. Do not use 不. To ask, add 吗: 你去过中国吗？
Compare 了 and 过: 我去了中国 says the trip happened; 我去过中国 says it is part of your experience. To say how many times, put it after 过: 我去过三次中国.

examples.en: I have been to China.
Have you ever drunk black tea?
I have never learned to swim.
He has seen this movie twice.

mistakes: Do not use 不 with 过. 我不去过中国 is wrong; say 我没去过中国 (I have never been to China).

q.en: I have eaten fish.
q.explain: Verb + 过 shows you have done it before.

q.en: He has never been abroad.
q.explain: 没 + verb + 过.

q.en: Have you seen this movie?
q.explain: 过 goes straight after the verb.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I have never drunk coffee?
q.en: I have never drunk coffee.
q.explain: Use 没, not 不, with 过.

q.en: Have you studied Chinese before?
q.explain: Verb + 过, then 吗 for the question.

title: 着: a state that continues
explain: Put 着 after a verb to describe a state that is still there: 门开着 'The door is open'; 他站着，我坐着 'He is standing and I am sitting'. It shows how things are right now.
着 can also link two actions: the first, with 着, shows how the second is done. 他笑着说话 'He talks with a smile'; 弟弟坐着看电视 'My younger brother watches TV sitting down'.
To say it is not in that state, drop 着 and use 没: 门没开 'The door is not open'. For an action in progress use 在 or 正在 (他在跑步 'He is running'); 着 describes a state, like 门开着.

examples.en: The door is open.
He is standing and I am sitting.
The phone is on.
He talks with a smile.

mistakes: 着 describes a state, not an action in progress. For 'is running' say 他在跑步, and use 着 for things like 门开着.

q.en: A boy is standing at the door.
q.explain: Place + verb + 着 + who or what is there.

q.en: The phone is on.
q.explain: Verb + 着 keeps the state.

q.en: He talks with a smile.
q.explain: 着 sits right after the first verb.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The restaurant door is open?
q.en: The restaurant door is open.
q.explain: Do not put 了 and 着 together on the same verb.

q.en: My younger brother watches TV sitting down.
q.explain: 着 shows how he watches.

title: 快要 and 就要: something is about to happen
explain: 快要…了, 就要…了 and 要…了 all mean 'is about to': 快要下雨了 'It is about to rain'; 我们要出门了 'We are about to go out'. The 了 at the end is needed.
快 on its own also works: 快下雨了.
With a time word, use 就要, not 快要: 他明天就要走了 'He is leaving tomorrow'; 后天就要考试了 'The exam is the day after tomorrow'.

examples.en: It is about to rain.
We are about to go out.
He is leaving tomorrow.
The exam is coming up, so I need to get ready.

mistakes: Do not put a specific time before 快要. 明天快要考试了 is wrong; say 明天就要考试了.

q.en: The bus is about to come.
q.explain: 快要 + verb + 了.

q.en: The teacher is about to come in.
q.explain: 就要 + verb + 了.

q.en: Dad is coming back the day after tomorrow.
q.explain: With a time word (后天) use 就要.

q.en: The exam is the day after tomorrow.
q.explain: 快要 cannot follow a specific time; 就要 can.

q.en: Dinner is almost ready.
q.explain: 快要 + adjective + 了 also works.

title: 已经…了 and 就: already, and sooner than expected
explain: 已经…了 means 'already': 我已经吃饭了 'I have already eaten'. 已经 goes before the verb and 了 comes at the end (or right after the verb).
就 before a verb can mean 'as early as' or 'right away': 我五点就起床了 'I got up as early as five'; 他八点就到了 'He was already there by eight'. Use 就 when something is earlier or quicker than you expected.
就 can also mean 'then, in that case': 你累了，就休息吧 'If you are tired, rest then'.

examples.en: I have already eaten.
He has already left.
I got up as early as five.
If you are tired, then rest.

mistakes: Do not use 已经 with something that has not happened. For 'not yet' say 还没: 我还没吃饭 'I have not eaten yet', not 我已经没吃饭.

q.en: She has already gone home.
q.explain: 已经 goes before the verb, 了 at the end.

q.en: We were at school by eight.
q.explain: 就 goes before the verb and shows it was early.

q.en: My younger brother has already eaten.
q.explain: 已经 + verb + 了.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I have not eaten yet?
q.en: I have not eaten yet.
q.explain: Use 还没 for not yet; 已经 does not go with 没.

q.en: He got up as early as five, so early.
q.explain: 就 shows it happened earlier than expected.

title: 让 and 别: letting, asking and telling not to
explain: 让 means 'to let' or 'to ask someone to': 他让我等一会儿 'He asked me to wait a moment'; 妈妈让我早点睡觉 'Mom tells me to go to bed early'. The person comes right after 让.
让 can also mean 'to make': 这个电影让我很高兴 'This movie made me happy'.
别 + verb tells someone not to do something: 别走 'Do not go'; 别说话 'Do not talk'. 别…了 asks someone to stop: 别笑了 'Stop laughing'. 别 means the same as 不要 but is more common in speech.

examples.en: Mom tells me to go to bed early.
He asked me to wait a moment.
This movie makes me happy.
Do not go; sit a little longer.

mistakes: Do not leave out the person after 让. You need 让 + who + what: 妈妈让我早点睡觉.

q.en: The teacher asked us to come in.
q.explain: 让 + who + what.

q.en: Do not make phone calls here.
q.explain: 别 + verb.

q.en: Dad asks me to go and buy medicine.
q.explain: 让 + who + what.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Do not go in?
q.en: Do not go in.
q.explain: 别 tells someone not to; 没 says it did not happen.

q.en: Stop talking, I am busy.
q.explain: 别…了 asks someone to stop.

title: 因为…所以… and 虽然…但是…
explain: 因为 gives the reason and 所以 gives the result: 因为下雨，所以我们在家看电影 'Because it is raining, we watch a movie at home'. In English you use only one of 'because' and 'so'; Chinese can use both. You can also drop either: 因为下雨，我们在家 and 下雨，所以我们在家 are both fine.
虽然 'although' and 但是 'but' come as a pair too: 虽然很累，但是我很高兴 'Although I am tired, I am happy'. English does not say 'although … but', and Chinese needs a 'but' word (但是, or just 但) in the second part.
为什么 asks for the reason: 你为什么不去？ 'Why are you not going?' The answer starts with 因为.

examples.zh: 因为下雨，所以我们在家看电影。
examples.en: Because it is raining, we watch a movie at home.

examples.zh: 因为今天很冷，所以我不想出门。
examples.en: Because it is cold today, I do not want to go out.

examples.zh: 虽然这个很贵，但是很好。
examples.en: Although this one is expensive, it is good.
Why are you not going?

mistakes: After 虽然, add a 'but' word (但是 or 但) in the second part, the way Chinese does: 虽然很累，但是很高兴.

q.zh: 因为太晚了，所以我回家了。
q.en: Because it was too late, I went home.
q.explain: 因为 gives the reason, 所以 the result.

q.zh: 虽然很远，但是我走路去。
q.en: Although it is far, I walk there.
q.explain: 虽然 pairs with 但是.

q.en: Because it is raining, I am not going.
q.explain: 因为 introduces the reason.

q.zh: 虽然他很小，但是他懂很多。
q.en: Although he is young, he understands a lot.
q.explain: 虽然 is answered by 但是.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Although it is cold, I am happy?
options: 虽然很冷，但是我很高兴。
虽然很冷，因为我很高兴。
q.zh: 虽然很冷，但是我很高兴。
q.en: Although it is cold, I am happy.
q.explain: 虽然 pairs with 但是, not 因为.
